title: Do Multimodal Agents Really Benefit from Tool Use? A Systematic Study of Capability Gains
abstract: arXiv:2606.02357v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Tool-augmented multimodal agents show strong benchmark gains, often taken as evidence that agents have learned to use tools. We argue that this interpretation can be premature: a tool-call trace alone does not show whether the tool supplied answer-critical information. We study two representative ``thinking with images'' agents, Thyme and DeepEyesV2, across real-world understanding, OCR, chart understanding, and mathematical reasoning. Each agent is compared with its Tool-Free counterpart and with a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from the same source pool without tool-calling trajectories. Tool access yields little consistent aggregate improvement, does not reliably reduce generated-token cost, and leaves only a small tool-only solved set: 93% of DeepEyesV2's tool-solved problems and 96% of Thyme's are also solved by at least one non-tool setting. translated_title: 多模态智能体真的从工具使用中获益吗？能力增益的系统性研究
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.02357v2 公告类型：跨领域替换 摘要：工具增强的多模态智能体在基准测试中表现出显著提升，这常被视为智能体已学会使用工具的证据。我们认为这种解读可能为时过早：仅凭工具调用轨迹并不能证明工具提供了答案关键信息。我们研究了两个代表性的“图像思考”智能体，Thyme和DeepEyesV2，覆盖真实世界理解、OCR、图表理解和数学推理任务。每个智能体与其无工具版本以及从相同源池训练、无工具调用轨迹的纯文本推理器进行比较。工具访问带来的一致性总体改进很小，不能可靠地降低生成令牌成本，且仅留下少量仅工具可解的问题集：DeepEyesV2的93%工具可解问题和Thyme的96%工具可解问题也至少被一种无工具设置解决。机制消融进一步表明，完整的工具使用循环并非始终优于简化替代方案。
tldr: 系统性研究表明，多模态智能体的工具使用并未带来显著能力提升，大多数工具可解问题无需工具也能解决，挑战了工具增强有效性的普遍假设。
en_tdlr: A systematic study reveals that tool use in multimodal agents yields minimal capability gains, with most tool-solvable problems also solvable without tools, challenging the common assumption of tool-augmentation effectiveness.
